heuristic.applicability: Prefer for the full early-to-late skill when uncertainty is chiefly which demonstrated phase is active: still holding/releasing the lid, open approach, near-peg closure, or carrying lift. Observable two-frame geometry and motion must remain within successful-demonstration support.

handoff.entry_conditions: Either the fingers are still coupled to the observed lid handle near the open-lid boundary, or the lid is released and the peg remains in the box. Two causal frames must be available across the switch.
handoff.exit_conditions: Closed fingers, peg above the box rim, and peg/TCP co-motion indicate readiness; this policy may continue into initial turn through index 1270.
handoff.failure_signatures: The inferred phase is inconsistent with geometry (for example, returning to lid while open near peg); premature close; descent while still near the lid handle; stationary peg under lift; changing peg/TCP offset; wall-stalled motion; or persistent IK residual/limits.
handoff.overlap_role: Explicit phase observables are trained on every action in [740,950) and [1120,1270), preserving robust early and late switches rather than narrowing to the central grasp.
handoff.successor_readiness: The successor is ready when explicit causal features agree: fingers are closed, peg is above the wall, and the last two frames show peg/TCP co-motion. This remains guidance because no contact truth is available.

heuristic.limitations: World-absolute targets preserve demonstrated robot/world geometry and can extrapolate poorly when peg position moves beyond support; the peg-frame prior is the displacement specialist. Deterministic phase cues are not contact truth and successful demonstrations provide no failed-grasp negatives. Co-motion over two frames can be ambiguous while stationary. This policy cannot establish grasp success, recover a drop, or guarantee lid/box collision avoidance. Absolute Cartesian targets may be unreachable from substantially changed qpos; the current-TCP policy better addresses modest hand-state offsets.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use as the broad phase-disambiguation/default policy, particularly for early lid-held entries. Prefer the peg-frame policy once the lid is observably released and peg displacement dominates, or the local-increment policy when hand configuration mismatch dominates. Terminate only on combined closed-finger, height, and co-motion cues; do not equate a phase feature or negative gripper command with contact.
heuristic.rationale: The demonstrations include a discrete active-object and gripper transition: demo12200 holds the lid at 740-750, opens at 760-770, clears at 800-950, descends at 990-1080, closes at 1100, and lifts at 1120-1240. The same ordering occurs in demo12208 despite a shifted peg and different lift timing. Mechanism: retain a world-absolute Cartesian target (position, 6-D rotation, gripper), but construct causal inputs around explicit transferable phase observables: TCP relative to peg, TCP relative to the kinematically computed lid handle, finger width/opening change, peg height above box wall, two-frame peg/TCP relative-pose change, lid angle/velocity, and qpos/qvel. The unchanged diffusion backbone sees these cues plus world poses. This should reduce aliasing between visually/geometrically similar portions while retaining world reachability context. It targets phase errors rather than displacement or local-state errors.
heuristic.statement: Phase-observable world-Cartesian prior for active-object and grasp/lift ambiguity.
